developer_request: Take over this existing project and determine whether its green behavioral tests actually prove the Runtime behavior before relying on them for completion or release decisions.
known_facts: The project contains tests that correctly call ContextEngine for some mode-selection scenarios, so the test files are not wholly fake.

The same embodied-learning-loop test file also assigns actual_dims = expected_dims and then asserts equality, so that result cannot change when the production Runtime state-vector implementation changes.
The same file checks expected_steps == STEPS_BY_MODE[mode], which compares the test's local expected table to itself instead of observing the Runtime ExecutionPlan.
The parent-reply test defines QUICK_SCAN and ALL_FM locally and verifies those local sets directly instead of asking MingOSRuntime which failure modes an actual quick/standard/deep plan will scan.
These checks can execute, be discovered distinctly, and propagate failures correctly while still providing no implementation-path evidence for the behavior they claim to verify.
expected_first_moves: separate tests that call the authoritative implementation from tests that only validate local mirrored constants or shadow logic
narrow the evidence scope of self-comparison tests to specification/reference consistency rather than implementation/runtime proof
replace or supplement material behavioral checks with assertions whose observed actual values come from the authoritative Runtime/implementation path
when consequence is material, demonstrate mutation sensitivity or an equivalent causal dependency so a relevant implementation defect can make the verification fail
recompute acceptance evidence after fixing the verification target instead of preserving a historical green count
must_preserve: useful specification/reference fixtures that are honestly scoped
the distinction between a test-target defect and an implementation defect
the project's domain-specific mode, safety, and response contracts unless direct product evidence independently requires a change
must_not: treat a test as implementation proof merely because it executes and exits zero
promote actual-equals-expected self-assignment or mirrored constants into runtime evidence
delete useful contract fixtures solely because they are not implementation tests
change product behavior merely to preserve a large historical pass count
turn this consumer's Python constants, module names, or MingOS domain semantics into AAOP Core rules
lessons: Verification integrity includes evidence-target fidelity: a passing assertion must observe the implementation or runtime surface it claims to prove, not merely a mirrored representation in the test itself.

Harness discovery, execution, and failure propagation can all be correct while the resulting evidence is still weak because the asserted actual value has no causal dependency on the owning implementation.
Shadow implementations and mirrored constants may remain valuable as specification/reference checks, but their claim scope must stay narrower than implementation or runtime verification.
A representative mutation-sensitive path is a practical way to prove that material verification can detect relevant implementation drift.
